questions.question: What does bounding-box IoU divide the intersection area by?
options: The union area of the two boxes
The sum of their center coordinates
The larger box's perimeter
The number of tracker frames
questions.explanation: IoU is intersection over union, so overlapping area is normalized by the area covered by either box.

questions.question: How does the tracker turn IoU into a Hungarian assignment cost?
options: It uses IoU directly and rewards every invalid pair
It uses 1-IoU and gives very large cost to invalid low-IoU pairs
It uses the box perimeter as the only cost
It assigns every detection to the oldest track
questions.explanation: Higher overlap should mean lower cost; pairs below the configured overlap threshold are discouraged with a large sentinel cost.

questions.question: With match_iou_threshold=0.3, which pair is considered geometrically valid?
options: A pair with IoU below 0.3
Only a pair whose boxes are identical
A pair with IoU at least 0.3
A pair chosen without looking at IoU
questions.explanation: The tracker accepts an assignment when its overlap reaches the threshold; lower-overlap matches are treated as invalid.

questions.question: What does a track's max_age measure?
options: The maximum width of its bounding box
The number of classes in the detector
The age of the video file on disk
How many frames it may remain unmatched before removal
questions.explanation: Each missed update increases the track's age, and max_age controls how long that missing track is retained.

questions.question: What happens to a detection that cannot be matched to an existing track?
options: The tracker creates a new Track with a new ID
It is assigned the first track's ID automatically
It is used only to change the frame rate
It is discarded even when new-track creation is enabled
questions.explanation: Unmatched detections represent possible new objects, so the implementation starts tracks for them.

questions.question: When does count_id_switches report an ID switch?
options: A frame contains two detections of different objects
The same ground-truth object is associated with a different tracker ID later
A track survives a missed frame
A bounding box has zero area
questions.explanation: An ID switch measures identity inconsistency over time, not simply the presence of multiple objects or missed detections.
